subject.title: [Feature]: Support for sandbox Docker parameters (--gpus all, --ipc=host)

question: Should OpenClaw add a narrow host IPC Docker sandbox option, reject host IPC, or design a broader dangerous Docker namespace policy first?
rationale: Host IPC changes the sandbox isolation boundary, and the repository already treats Docker namespace joins and dangerous sandbox options as explicit security decisions rather than automation-only fixes.

options.title: Add narrow host IPC field
options.body: Add an explicit opt-in IPC setting with schema, docs, config hashing, create-args, security-audit coverage, and warnings, while keeping raw Docker args unsupported.

options.title: Reject Host IPC
options.body: Keep Docker sandbox isolation tighter and close the host IPC portion as unsupported, leaving GPU passthrough as the supported high-power workload path.

options.title: Design Broader Namespace Policy
options.body: Pause implementation until maintainers define a consistent policy for IPC, PID, network namespace joins, and related dangerous Docker options.

recommendation.title: Add narrow host IPC field
recommendation.body: Add an explicit opt-in IPC setting with schema, docs, config hashing, create-args, security-audit coverage, and warnings, while keeping raw Docker args unsupported.

likelyOwner.reason: CODEOWNERS owns the sandbox and security-sensitive paths affected by this boundary decision.
